prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where a current General Authority Seventy served as a young full-time missionary.
prompts.text_original: Many General Authority Seventies serving as of October 2026 were once young full-time missionaries. Pin a European country where one of them served that mission, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Before their calls as General Authorities, many Seventies served as young missionaries abroad. As of October 2026, their biographies name European missions in England, Scotland, Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, Portugal, Russia, Finland and the Czech Republic.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: England Manchester, London East and London South; Scotland Edinburgh missions (Elders Phillips, Boom, Hirst, Holland).

answers.name: Germany

answers.name: France

answers.name: Switzerland

answers.name: Spain

answers.name: Italy

answers.name: Portugal

answers.name: Russia

answers.name: Czech Republic

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding the homeland of a people in the Psalm 83 confederacy against Israel
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding the homeland of a people in the confederacy against Israel in Psalm 83:6-11 (Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines, Tyre, Assur), or a people or place the psalm recalls from earlier victories (Midian, the brook Kison, En-dor)
prompts.note: Philistine Gaza is in Palestine; Philistine Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath are in Israel, so both count.
prompts.summary: Psalm 83, a psalm of Asaph, describes nations that took crafty counsel to cut Israel off: Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines and Tyre, helped by Assur. The psalmist asks the Lord to deal with them as with Midian and with Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kison (Ps 83).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and Ammon are in the confederacy (Ps 83:6-7).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Assur also is joined with them (Ps 83:8).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The psalm recalls Sisera and Jabin at the brook of Kison, who perished at En-dor (Ps 83:9-10).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The inhabitants of Tyre join the confederacy (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The Philistines are in the confederacy; their city Gaza is in the Gaza Strip (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: The psalm recalls the Midianites (Ps 83:9); Church Bible Map 9 plots Midian east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Amalek is in the confederacy (Ps 83:7); Church Bible Map 2 places Israel's first battle with Amalek at Rephidim in the Sinai (Ex 17:8-16).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a kingdom or battle site in the war of the kings, Genesis 14
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a kingdom or battle site in the war of the kings in Genesis 14: the eastern kings of Shinar and Elam, the peoples they smote from Ashteroth Karnaim to mount Seir and El-paran, the vale of Siddim by the salt sea, and Abram's pursuit to Dan and Hobah near Damascus
prompts.note: The salt sea (Dead Sea) is shared by Israel, Jordan and the West Bank, so all three count for the vale of Siddim.
prompts.summary: Four eastern kings led by Chedorlaomer of Elam crushed a revolt by five cities of the plain, swept through Bashan, Moab, Seir and Kadesh, and carried Lot away from Sodom. Abram armed 318 servants, pursued them to Dan and beyond Damascus, rescued Lot, and paid tithes to Melchizedek king of Salem (Gen 14).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Amraphel was king of Shinar, the land of Babylon (Gen 14:1).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The kings smote the Amorites at Hazezon-tamar, which is Engedi, and Abram pursued them unto Dan (Gen 14:7, 14; 2 Chr 20:2).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Chedorlaomer, who led the war, was king of Elam (Gen 14:1, 4-5).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: They smote the Zuzims in Ham and the Horites in their mount Seir (Gen 14:5-6).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: They smote the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and Abram chased them to Hobah, on the left hand of Damascus (Gen 14:5, 15).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The Horites were smitten in mount Seir unto El-paran, the wilderness of Paran in the central Sinai peninsula (Gen 14:6; Bible Dictionary, Paran).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The battle was in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea (Gen 14:3); the Dead Sea's northwest shore is in the West Bank.
